name: Bikan Historical Quarter
tagline: Willow-lined canals and Edo-era rice storehouses
description: Kurashiki's postcard heart, white-walled kura warehouses and black-tiled merchant houses lining a willow-shaded canal, with the Ohara Museum of Art at its center. Beautiful and genuinely historic, but thick with day-trippers and tour buses from mid-morning until late afternoon, quieting down and turning atmospheric again in the evening once shops close.
vibe: postcard-historic, touristy by day, quiet by night
pros: Ohara Museum and canal boat rides on site

name: Kurashiki Station Area
tagline: The practical, everyday base for getting around
description: The commercial hub around JR Kurashiki Station, anchored by the Tenmaya department store, Ario Kurashiki mall, and a cluster of chain cafes with reliable wifi. Less charming than the Bikan quarter but far more convenient for daily errands, transit connections to Okayama, and reasonably priced apartments a short walk or bike ride from the historic center.
bestFor: remote workers, longer stays, budget-conscious renters
pros: direct rail access to Okayama and beyond
chain cafes with wifi for working
cons: quiet at night outside the mall

name: Achi / Ivy Square
tagline: A converted 19th-century textile mill turned cultural quarter
description: Just southeast of the main Bikan canal, this area centers on Kurashiki Ivy Square, a red-brick former spinning mill now home to a hotel, restaurants, and small museums, alongside Achi Shrine on the hill above with sweeping views over the old town. A calmer alternative to the canal's busiest stretch while staying walking distance from everything.
pros: Achi Shrine viewpoint over the old town
still close to Bikan on foot

name: Kojima (Jeans Street)
tagline: Japan's denim birthplace, a laid-back coastal district
description: A distinct district south of central Kurashiki, Kojima is where Japan's domestic denim industry began, and its Jeans Street is lined with denim boutiques, workshops, and small cafes in a relaxed, un-touristy setting. It sits near the Seto Ohashi bridge and coastline, offering a different, more local pace than the historic center, though it requires a train or drive to reach.
bestFor: denim and craft enthusiasts, day trips, quieter living
